z: 亣 ingqe, isihlakala, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
A child does not need a conversation performed. A child needs a person who can be found. Being findable is the practice. The words can come later, or not.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 亣 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: If your quiet has been a punishment, break it with one gentle sentence and then stay.

z: 产 ingqe, isihlakala, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Forgiveness does not require the betrayed to be foolish. It requires them to decide whether the person is still a member. Membership is a practice after it has been a wound.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 产 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: If you were the one who broke trust, say what you did without a speech about why it was almost fair.

z: 亩 ingqe, isihlakala, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
A marriage that has lost a child, or a parent, or a future, needs presence more than explanation. Explanation is a way of leaving. Sitting is a way of staying.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 亩 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Answer the ordinary request of a grieving child. Do not make them perform a sadness you recognize.

z: 亪 ingqe, isihlakala, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
A marriage in despair does not need a speech about gratitude. It needs one true plan for tomorrow that both people can bear. Make the plan small enough to be kept.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 亪 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Decline the word forever. Keep the true sentence about the pain, and stop before the lie.

z: 亯 ingqe, isihlakala, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
In a marriage, revenge is often petty and therefore easy to excuse. The small cut, repeated, is how love is replaced by a contest. Mercy is leaving one cut unanswered.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 亯 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Tell the truth of the wrong once, to the person, and then do not serve it at breakfast.

z: 亱 ingqe, isihlakala, phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Accountability begins when you can say, the heat was mine. Wisdom begins when you can say, it had a better door. Compassion begins when the person you nearly burned is still in the room, and you stay.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, phezulu, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 亱 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: If you have already burned someone you love, say so before the day ends, and then do one ordinary kindness with your hands.

z: 亲 ingqe, isihlakala, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Self-reflection is the moment you notice you needed to win. Accountability is saying so before you are forced. The turn from pride to dignity is mostly this small honesty.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 亲 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Kneel, or sit, so your eyes meet a child's. Stay there until the conversation is theirs.

z: 亴 ingqe, isihlakala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Siblings are assigned the same story and different gifts. Envy calls this injustice. Admiration calls it a house with more than one lamp. Both lamps belong on the table.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 亴 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Ask the person to show you how they did the thing. Be a student for ten minutes.

z: 亵 ingqe, isihlakala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Many houses, under many names, give the same command: do not be ruled by dread, and do not despise the person who is. The strong are asked to stay, not to sneer.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 亵 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Hold the doorway. Let the frightened one see that you are not leaving.

z: 亷 ingqe, isihlakala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Hospitality is the oldest sociology of the lasting house. The stranger eats first. The family that cannot do this for a guest will eventually fail to do it for itself.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 亷 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Give a thing away that you still like. Do not wait until you are tired of it.

z: 亸 ingqe, isihlakala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Siblings remember the name they were called on the worst day. Do not give them that name. Give them the name of the good you have actually seen them do.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 亸 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Tell one story tonight in which a person in this house is repaired, not mocked.

z: 亽 ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Children who are met with contempt learn to hide the clumsy part, which is most of them. Appreciation gives that part a chair.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 亽 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Ask to be shown a skill you had decided was beneath you. Watch the whole way through.

z: 亾 ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
The old practice of sitting with the sick, of keeping watch, of not filling the air, is this turn. Do not rush to be useful. Be there.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 亾 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Be findable. Tell the house which room you will be in, and be in it.

z: 亿 ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
The wisdom shared by many houses is hard: do not let the sun go down on a break you are willing to heal, and do not call it healing if you are only waiting to retell it.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 亿 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Decide, and say, whether the person is still a member. Do not leave them in a fog.

z: 仅 ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Children grieve in strange hours and then ask for ordinary things. Both are grief. Answer the ordinary thing. Do not make them perform a sadness you can recognize.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 仅 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Leave the empty place unspoken-of only if the grieving person wishes it. Otherwise, speak the name.

z: 仉 ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
A child who sees an adult look again, after a bad day, learns that a bad day is not a verdict. This is worth more than any optimism you could announce.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 仉 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Set one place at the table that despair said was pointless. Eat there.

z: 仌 ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Children are the usual casualties of a score kept between adults. They did not agree to carry it. Mercy toward the person you resent is also protection of the child.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 仌 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Do one undeserved kindness where you are keeping score. Do not mention the score.

z: 仑 ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Siblings fight because they share a roof and a hunger. The fight is not the failure. The failure is when the stronger one discovers a liking for the smaller one's fear. Protection refuses that discovery.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 仑 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: When the heat rises, name who you are actually keeping safe. Put your body between the danger and the child. Do not spend the heat on the child.

z: 仒 ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Brothers and sisters are the first public. What you do to be admired at home becomes the way they will treat their own children. Give them a dignity they can copy.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 仒 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Once, take the lower seat on purpose. Let someone in the house finish a story you could have told better.

z: 仓 ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
The teachings that endured all warn the eye. They also bless the eye that rejoices. Rejoicing is not a mood. It is a decision made again each time the other person shines.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 仓 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Say out loud, in the hearing of the person, the exact good you wished were yours. Then leave it theirs.

z: 仛 ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Fear of the future makes a house small. Courage does not enlarge the future. It keeps today's people inside the house while the future remains unknown.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 仛 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Stay until the scared person is breathing slowly. Do not explain the dark away before you have sat in it.

z: 仜 ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Psychology is simple here. The closed hand teaches the body that the world is about to run out. The open hand teaches it that tomorrow includes other people.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 仜 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Pass the best portion first. The first piece teaches the house what it is.

z: 仠 ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Gossip is how a house talks about its own when they have left the room. Healing speech waits until they are back, and then says the hard thing to the face, cleanly.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 仠 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Speak the true sentence. Keep the second one, the one that only wanted to win.

z: 仢 ingqe, isihlakala, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Across the old writings, the warning against scoffing is constant. A scoffer cannot be taught, and a house that scoffs cannot learn itself.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 仢 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Look at one ordinary object they mended or prepared, and say what it cost them.

z: 仦 ingqe, isihlakala, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Some truths are not ready for speech. Presence holds them without using them as a weapon. A weaponized silence is still a weapon.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 仦 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: If your quiet has been a punishment, break it with one gentle sentence and then stay.

z: 仧 ingqe, isihlakala, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
A child who watches a break become a lifelong trial learns that love is a court. A child who watches a break become a mended bowl learns that love can survive its own failure.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 仧 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: If you were the one who broke trust, say what you did without a speech about why it was almost fair.

z: 仨 ingqe, isihlakala, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Compassion is grief that has recognized itself in another body and does not hurry it. Hurry is fear. The unhurried hour is the gift.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 仨 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Bring food. Take the lower seat. Stay past the moment you become uncomfortable.

z: 仩 ingqe, isihlakala, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
The sciences of a lasting household call this resilience. The older word is faithfulness. It does not deny the dark. It refuses to let the dark be the only speaker.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 仩 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Make one plan for tomorrow small enough that both of you can keep it.

z: 仪 ingqe, isihlakala, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Many sacred traditions, in different grammars, say the same hard thing: the injury stops when someone declines to pass it on. This is not weakness. It is the end of a chain.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 仪 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Leave one cut unanswered today. Do not announce the leaving.

z: 们 ingqe, isihlakala, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
At the table, anger wants the last word. The last word is rarely food. Let the sentence end before it becomes the story the children will tell about this house.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 们 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Before the second loud sentence, step into the doorway, not toward the person. Let the heat guard the house from outside.

z: 仯 ingqe, isihlakala, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The guest at the table is a test you did not schedule. If your worth requires the guest to be less clever, less beautiful, less faithful, your worth is a costume. Take it off.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at ingqe, isihlakala, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 仯 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Kneel, or sit, so your eyes meet a child's. Stay there until the conversation is theirs.

z: 仳 intende yesandla, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
What you wish were yours, name it exactly, in the hearing of the person who has it. Then do not reach. The naming is the confession. The not-reaching is the turn.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at intende yesandla, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 仳 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Ask the person to show you how they did the thing. Be a student for ten minutes.

z: 仴 intende yesandla, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Name the loss you are counting. Often it is a person in the room, not a disaster outside. Then put your body beside that person. That is the whole practice.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at intende yesandla, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 仴 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Hold the doorway. Let the frightened one see that you are not leaving.

z: 仸 intende yesandla, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Give before you calculate whether you will be thanked. Thanks are not the food. If you require them, you have made a trade, and a trade is not yet a family.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at intende yesandla, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 仸 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Feed the guest, or the youngest, before you take your own share.

z: 仹 intende yesandla, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Wisdom is not silence forever. There is a time to speak. The test is whether the words can be repeated in front of the person, and still be a kindness.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at intende yesandla, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 仹 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Say the hard thing to the face, once, cleanly, with no audience.

z: 仺 intende yesandla, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Look at the work you have stopped seeing. Name it. The naming is not flattery. It is the return of sight, and sight is the turn.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at intende yesandla, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 仺 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Remove the sneer from a sentence and speak it again. Notice how much of it was only the sneer.

z: 仾 intende yesandla, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Put the glowing thing in another room. Sit where you can be seen. You do not have to be interesting. You do have to be in the house.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at intende yesandla, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 仾 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Sit with a person who is not ready to speak. Let ten minutes pass without fixing them.

z: 伂 intende yesandla, phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Accountability is the first half. Without it, forgiveness is a fog. The one who broke the trust says what was done, without a speech about why it was almost justified.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at intende yesandla, phezulu, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 伂 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Decide, and say, whether the person is still a member. Do not leave them in a fog.

z: 伄 intende yesandla, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The oldest writings are full of lament, not because lament is holy by itself, but because love that cannot lament becomes hard. Let the house be soft enough to cry.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at intende yesandla, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 伄 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Leave the empty place unspoken-of only if the grieving person wishes it. Otherwise, speak the name.

z: 伅 intende yesandla, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Despair often tells the truth about pain and then adds a lie about forever. Keep the truth. Decline the forever. Forever is not a fact available to a person at a window.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at intende yesandla, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 伅 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Set one place at the table that despair said was pointless. Eat there.

z: 伆 intende yesandla, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Accountability remains. Mercy is not the cancellation of truth. It is the decision that truth will not be used as a knife at breakfast for the next twenty years.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at intende yesandla, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 伆 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: If a child is carrying a feud that belongs to adults, take it back. Say that it is not theirs.

z: 伇 intende yesandla, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
An elder who has turned anger into protection does not become mild. The wall is still warm. What changes is the face it turns toward. It faces the street, not the cradle.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at intende yesandla, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 伇 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Teach the strong child to stand in front of the smaller one. That is anger, turned, and it can be learned young.

z: 伈 intende yesandla, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
An elder's dignity is not the right to be obeyed in every small thing. It is the right to be respected while still listening. The listening is what makes the respect true.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at intende yesandla, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 伈 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Praise a person in the house for a quality you do not share. Do not add a correction.

z: 伌 intende yesandla, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Across generations, envy of the young is fear of being finished. Admiration of the young is how an elder stays in the story without owning it.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at intende yesandla, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 伌 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: When a sibling is praised, add one true sentence of your own. Do not balance it with your own news.

z: 伒 intende yesandla, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
An elder who has been afraid and stayed is a better teacher than an elder who claims never to have shaken. The shaking, survived, is the lesson.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at intende yesandla, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 伒 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Stay until the scared person is breathing slowly. Do not explain the dark away before you have sat in it.

z: 伓 intende yesandla, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
An elder who gives the best piece away is not being careless with the future. The elder is showing the future how a house continues.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at intende yesandla, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 伓 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Pass the best portion first. The first piece teaches the house what it is.

z: 伔 intende yesandla, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
An elder's stories are a kind of speech that builds or bends a family. Tell the story in which people are repaired. The other story will tell itself.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at intende yesandla, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 伔 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Speak the true sentence. Keep the second one, the one that only wanted to win.

z: 伕 intende yesandla, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
An elder who still notices the small faithfulness in the house is a gift to the young. The young become what is noticed.

This is the work of an elder with the young. Look long enough at intende yesandla, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 伕 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Thank a person for a labor you have stopped seeing. Thank the labor, not their temperament.

z: 众 intende yesandla, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
An elder's quiet can be a shelter or a locked door. The young can tell which, by whether they are welcome to come and say nothing beside you.

z: 伟 intende yesandla, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla

line:
Pride needs an audience and a person beneath it. Dignity needs neither. Hidden inside pride is the refusal to be nothing. That refusal is good. It becomes poison only when someone else must be smaller for it to stand.

line:
Envy is love of a good thing, twisted until the good thing must shrink. The love was real. That is why it hurts. Turned, the same look becomes admiration, which is fed by another person's light.

line:
Fear is the mind counting what it loves and what it could lose. That count is not a defect. It is proof of attachment, and attachment is how a family exists. Courage is fear that stays in the room.

z: 伣 intende yesandla, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Greed is the fear that there will not be enough, wearing the mask of appetite. Bread kept in a closed hand goes stale. Generosity is the same hand remembering the table.

z: 伤 intende yesandla, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The tongue is the smallest member and the widest fire. Every tradition that lasted put a guard on it, because a family is made of sentences more than of walls.

practice: Say the hard thing to the face, once, cleanly, with no audience.

z: 伥 intende yesandla, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Contempt is a shortcut. It saves a person from having to look. Inside it is the power it refuses: the power to see a thing clearly. Clear sight is the beginning of thanks.

z: 伦 intende yesandla, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
There is a silence that punishes and a silence that accompanies. They use the same closed mouth. The difference is whether the person has left while remaining in the chair.

z: 伧 intende yesandla, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Betrayal proves that trust was real, because only a real bond breaks with that sound. Forgiveness is not the pretence that the bowl never cracked. It is gold in the crack, and the decision to eat from that bowl again, slowly.

z: 伨 intende yesandla, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Grief is love with nowhere to go. It feels like an evil because it stops the house. It is not an invader. It is a force large enough to be mistaken for one. Compassion is that force sitting down beside someone else.

line:
Despair says the dawn is a lie because the room is dark. The force inside it is the fact that someone is still at the window. Waiting is already a kind of faithfulness, even when it feels like defeat.

z: 伪 imithambo, umzwa, ithanga, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Revenge believes that pain can be balanced by being copied. It cannot. The copy multiplies, and the family becomes a ledger. Mercy is the refusal to become the injury.

z: 伫 imithambo, umzwa, ithanga, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
A marriage can survive a true no. It cannot survive a no that was only a wound looking for a second body. Protection is the no that guards the bond, not the no that wins the evening.

z: 伬 imithambo, umzwa, ithanga, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
A parent who comes down to a child's height does not lose rank. Rank was the costume. The person remains. Dignity is the choice to be seen without requiring worship.

practice: Praise a person in the house for a quality you do not share. Do not add a correction.

z: 伭 imithambo, umzwa, ithanga, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
A family that can clap for its own is already rich. The eye is the first thief, and it can be the first blessing. The difference is whether the good is allowed to remain in the other hand.

z: 伮 imithambo, umzwa, ithanga, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
The parent at the dark door does not stop being afraid. They stop leaving. Be with the frightened. Do not perform fearlessness. A performed bravery teaches a child to hide.

z: 伱 imithambo, umzwa, ithanga, phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Generosity is not the opposite of need. It is need that has remembered other mouths. The first portion, not the remainder, teaches the house what it is.

z: 伲 imithambo, umzwa, ithanga, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Healing speech is not sweetness. Sweetness can be a lie. Healing speech is accuracy with mercy. It names the hurt and refuses the insult that wanted to ride along.

line:
What is despised at home is despised twice, because home was the place it should have been safe to be plain. Appreciation is looking that did not turn away.

line:
Cold silence is absence wearing a body. Presence is that silence warmed by staying. Put the object down. Let the eyes finish the sentence the mouth is not ready to speak.

line:
A family that cannot mend becomes a set of strangers who still share a key. Mercy here is not amnesia. It is the refusal to make the break the only story the children inherit.

line:
The empty chair is not decorated away. The shawl is the theology. Every house that lasted taught its people to weep with those who weep, and only then to speak.

line:

line:

line:
Children learn what strength is from the body that stands between them and the weather. If that body spends itself on them, they learn that love arrives as weather. Turn the heat toward the actual danger.

z: 佄 imithambo, umzwa, ithanga, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
In a marriage, pride keeps a ledger of who apologized last. Dignity throws the ledger out and keeps the person. You can be wrong and still be whole.

line:
Between spouses, envy dresses as criticism. The dress is thin. Under it is the wish to be the one who is praised. Say the praise. Leave the gift where it landed.

In a marriage, fear says, if I tell the truth I will be left. Courage tells the truth and remains seated. The staying is the larger sentence.

A marriage becomes a grievance when the store is private. What is earned may be stewarded. What is hoarded becomes a wall between two people who share a bed.

line:
In a marriage, the second sentence is usually the one that only wanted to win. Speak the first, which is the truth. Keep the second. The keeping is love.

line:
A marriage dies faster from sneering than from anger. Anger still believes the other person matters. Contempt has already left, and only the body remains at the table.

line:
In a marriage, the punishing quiet can last longer than a blow, and it teaches the same lesson: you are alone in this room. Presence refuses to teach that.

Name the break once, plainly, without the extra charges that make you feel righteous. Then do one small trustworthy thing, and do it again tomorrow. Trust is rebuilt at that size.

The counsel that lasted did not flatter rage. It asked the strong to become a wall for the weak. That is the ethic of a parent and of an elder: your size is a shelter, or it is a threat.

line:
The old wisdom is severe on the high seat. It is not severe on the upright spine. Stand up. Then let the others stand. A house of one standing person is a court, not a family.

line:
A child who is envied by a parent carries a weight no child can name. Admiration from above is a kind of safety. It says, your becoming does not threaten my place.

z: 佭 imithambo, umzwa, ithanga, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
A child learns courage from a body that does not abandon the feeling. Sit until the breath slows. Explanation can wait. Presence cannot.

line:

z: 佱 imithambo, umzwa, ithanga, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
A child believes the sentence more than the apology that follows it. Speak as if the sentence will live in them, because it will. This is not fear. It is care.

z: 佲 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
The ordinary work, the meal, the repaired hinge, the repeated story, is the curriculum of a family. Thank the labor, not the performance of being easy to live with.

practice: Ask to be shown a skill you had decided was beneath you. Watch the whole way through.

z: 佴 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele

A child does not need a conversation performed. A child needs a person who can be found. Being findable is the practice. The words can come later, or not.

practice: Be findable. Tell the house which room you will be in, and be in it.

z: 佹 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Forgiveness does not require the betrayed to be foolish. It requires them to decide whether the person is still a member. Membership is a practice after it has been a wound.

practice: Decide, and say, whether the person is still a member. Do not leave them in a fog.

line:
A marriage that has lost a child, or a parent, or a future, needs presence more than explanation. Explanation is a way of leaving. Sitting is a way of staying.

practice: Leave the empty place unspoken-of only if the grieving person wishes it. Otherwise, speak the name.

line:
A marriage in despair does not need a speech about gratitude. It needs one true plan for tomorrow that both people can bear. Make the plan small enough to be kept.

practice: Set one place at the table that despair said was pointless. Eat there.

z: 侄 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
In a marriage, revenge is often petty and therefore easy to excuse. The small cut, repeated, is how love is replaced by a contest. Mercy is leaving one cut unanswered.

practice: Do one undeserved kindness where you are keeping score. Do not mention the score.

z: 侇 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Accountability begins when you can say, the heat was mine. Wisdom begins when you can say, it had a better door. Compassion begins when the person you nearly burned is still in the room, and you stay.

practice: When the heat rises, name who you are actually keeping safe. Put your body between the danger and the child. Do not spend the heat on the child.

z: 侉 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Self-reflection is the moment you notice you needed to win. Accountability is saying so before you are forced. The turn from pride to dignity is mostly this small honesty.

This is the work of an elder with the young. A successful family is a body that can still use every member. imithambo, imizwa, idolo, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu is included. 侉 is included. Neither is asked to disappear so the other can be admired.
practice: Once, take the lower seat on purpose. Let someone in the house finish a story you could have told better.

z: 侌 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Siblings are assigned the same story and different gifts. Envy calls this injustice. Admiration calls it a house with more than one lamp. Both lamps belong on the table.

This is the work of an elder with the young. A successful family is a body that can still use every member. imithambo, imizwa, idolo, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu is included. 侌 is included. Neither is asked to disappear so the other can be admired.
practice: Say out loud, in the hearing of the person, the exact good you wished were yours. Then leave it theirs.

z: 侎 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Many houses, under many names, give the same command: do not be ruled by dread, and do not despise the person who is. The strong are asked to stay, not to sneer.

This is the work of an elder with the young. A successful family is a body that can still use every member. imithambo, imizwa, idolo, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele is included. 侎 is included. Neither is asked to disappear so the other can be admired.
practice: Stay until the scared person is breathing slowly. Do not explain the dark away before you have sat in it.

z: 侐 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Hospitality is the oldest sociology of the lasting house. The stranger eats first. The family that cannot do this for a guest will eventually fail to do it for itself.

This is the work of an elder with the young. A successful family is a body that can still use every member. imithambo, imizwa, idolo, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla is included. 侐 is included. Neither is asked to disappear so the other can be admired.
practice: Pass the best portion first. The first piece teaches the house what it is.

z: 侓 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Siblings remember the name they were called on the worst day. Do not give them that name. Give them the name of the good you have actually seen them do.

This is the work of an elder with the young. A successful family is a body that can still use every member. imithambo, imizwa, idolo, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu is included. 侓 is included. Neither is asked to disappear so the other can be admired.
practice: Speak the true sentence. Keep the second one, the one that only wanted to win.

z: 侕 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Children who are met with contempt learn to hide the clumsy part, which is most of them. Appreciation gives that part a chair.

practice: Look at one ordinary object they mended or prepared, and say what it cost them.

z: 侙 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
The old practice of sitting with the sick, of keeping watch, of not filling the air, is this turn. Do not rush to be useful. Be there.

This is the work of an elder with the young. A successful family is a body that can still use every member. imithambo, imizwa, idolo, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele is included. 侙 is included. Neither is asked to disappear so the other can be admired.
practice: If your quiet has been a punishment, break it with one gentle sentence and then stay.

z: 侜 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
The wisdom shared by many houses is hard: do not let the sun go down on a break you are willing to heal, and do not call it healing if you are only waiting to retell it.

This is the work of an elder with the young. A successful family is a body that can still use every member. imithambo, imizwa, idolo, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla is included. 侜 is included. Neither is asked to disappear so the other can be admired.
practice: If you were the one who broke trust, say what you did without a speech about why it was almost fair.

z: 侞 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Children grieve in strange hours and then ask for ordinary things. Both are grief. Answer the ordinary thing. Do not make them perform a sadness you can recognize.

practice: Bring food. Take the lower seat. Stay past the moment you become uncomfortable.

z: 侟 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
A child who sees an adult look again, after a bad day, learns that a bad day is not a verdict. This is worth more than any optimism you could announce.

practice: Make one plan for tomorrow small enough that both of you can keep it.

z: 侢 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Children are the usual casualties of a score kept between adults. They did not agree to carry it. Mercy toward the person you resent is also protection of the child.

practice: Leave one cut unanswered today. Do not announce the leaving.

z: 侣 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Siblings fight because they share a roof and a hunger. The fight is not the failure. The failure is when the stronger one discovers a liking for the smaller one's fear. Protection refuses that discovery.

This is the work of an elder with the young. A successful family is a body that can still use every member. imithambo, imizwa, idolo, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla is included. 侣 is included. Neither is asked to disappear so the other can be admired.
practice: Before the second loud sentence, step into the doorway, not toward the person. Let the heat guard the house from outside.

z: 侤 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Brothers and sisters are the first public. What you do to be admired at home becomes the way they will treat their own children. Give them a dignity they can copy.

practice: Kneel, or sit, so your eyes meet a child's. Stay there until the conversation is theirs.

z: 侥 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
The teachings that endured all warn the eye. They also bless the eye that rejoices. Rejoicing is not a mood. It is a decision made again each time the other person shines.

practice: Ask the person to show you how they did the thing. Be a student for ten minutes.

z: 侦 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Fear of the future makes a house small. Courage does not enlarge the future. It keeps today's people inside the house while the future remains unknown.

This is the work of an elder with the young. A successful family is a body that can still use every member. imithambo, imizwa, idolo, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele is included. 侦 is included. Neither is asked to disappear so the other can be admired.
practice: Hold the doorway. Let the frightened one see that you are not leaving.

z: 侧 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Psychology is simple here. The closed hand teaches the body that the world is about to run out. The open hand teaches it that tomorrow includes other people.

practice: Feed the guest, or the youngest, before you take your own share.

z: 侨 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Gossip is how a house talks about its own when they have left the room. Healing speech waits until they are back, and then says the hard thing to the face, cleanly.

practice: Say the hard thing to the face, once, cleanly, with no audience.

z: 侩 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Across the old writings, the warning against scoffing is constant. A scoffer cannot be taught, and a house that scoffs cannot learn itself.

practice: Remove the sneer from a sentence and speak it again. Notice how much of it was only the sneer.

z: 侪 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Some truths are not ready for speech. Presence holds them without using them as a weapon. A weaponized silence is still a weapon.

practice: Sit with a person who is not ready to speak. Let ten minutes pass without fixing them.

z: 侬 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
A child who watches a break become a lifelong trial learns that love is a court. A child who watches a break become a mended bowl learns that love can survive its own failure.

This is the work of an elder with the young. A successful family is a body that can still use every member. imithambo, imizwa, idolo, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla is included. 侬 is included. Neither is asked to disappear so the other can be admired.
practice: Decide, and say, whether the person is still a member. Do not leave them in a fog.

z: 侰 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Compassion is grief that has recognized itself in another body and does not hurry it. Hurry is fear. The unhurried hour is the gift.

line:
The sciences of a lasting household call this resilience. The older word is faithfulness. It does not deny the dark. It refuses to let the dark be the only speaker.

practice: Set one place at the table that despair said was pointless. Eat there.

line:
Many sacred traditions, in different grammars, say the same hard thing: the injury stops when someone declines to pass it on. This is not weakness. It is the end of a chain.

practice: If a child is carrying a feud that belongs to adults, take it back. Say that it is not theirs.

z: 侴 imithambo, imizwa, idolo, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
At the table, anger wants the last word. The last word is rarely food. Let the sentence end before it becomes the story the children will tell about this house.

practice: Teach the strong child to stand in front of the smaller one. That is anger, turned, and it can be learned young.

line:
The guest at the table is a test you did not schedule. If your worth requires the guest to be less clever, less beautiful, less faithful, your worth is a costume. Take it off.

practice: Praise a person in the house for a quality you do not share. Do not add a correction.

What you wish were yours, name it exactly, in the hearing of the person who has it. Then do not reach. The naming is the confession. The not-reaching is the turn.

practice: When a sibling is praised, add one true sentence of your own. Do not balance it with your own news.

z: 侹 ngaphambili, umlenze, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Name the loss you are counting. Often it is a person in the room, not a disaster outside. Then put your body beside that person. That is the whole practice.

line:
Give before you calculate whether you will be thanked. Thanks are not the food. If you require them, you have made a trade, and a trade is not yet a family.

line:
Wisdom is not silence forever. There is a time to speak. The test is whether the words can be repeated in front of the person, and still be a kindness.

practice: Speak the true sentence. Keep the second one, the one that only wanted to win.

z: 侼 ngaphambili, umlenze, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Look at the work you have stopped seeing. Name it. The naming is not flattery. It is the return of sight, and sight is the turn.

practice: Thank a person for a labor you have stopped seeing. Thank the labor, not their temperament.

z: 侽 ngaphambili, umlenze, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Put the glowing thing in another room. Sit where you can be seen. You do not have to be interesting. You do have to be in the house.

practice: Put the glowing thing in another room. Sit where you can be seen. You do not have to perform a talk.

z: 俀 ngaphambili, umlenze, phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Accountability is the first half. Without it, forgiveness is a fog. The one who broke the trust says what was done, without a speech about why it was almost justified.

practice: Name the break once, without extra charges. Then do one small trustworthy thing, and repeat it tomorrow.

z: 俁 ngaphambili, umlenze, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The oldest writings are full of lament, not because lament is holy by itself, but because love that cannot lament becomes hard. Let the house be soft enough to cry.

practice: Do not hurry a grieving person into cheer. Let the absent name be said.

z: 俆 ngaphambili, umlenze, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Despair often tells the truth about pain and then adds a lie about forever. Keep the truth. Decline the forever. Forever is not a fact available to a person at a window.

practice: Make one plan for tomorrow small enough that both of you can keep it.

z: 俇 ngaphambili, umlenze, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Accountability remains. Mercy is not the cancellation of truth. It is the decision that truth will not be used as a knife at breakfast for the next twenty years.

practice: Leave one cut unanswered today. Do not announce the leaving.

z: 俈 ngaphambili, umlenze, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
An elder who has turned anger into protection does not become mild. The wall is still warm. What changes is the face it turns toward. It faces the street, not the cradle.

practice: Before the second loud sentence, step into the doorway, not toward the person. Let the heat guard the house from outside.

z: 俌 ngaphambili, umlenze, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
An elder's dignity is not the right to be obeyed in every small thing. It is the right to be respected while still listening. The listening is what makes the respect true.

This is the work of an elder with the young. A successful family is a body that can still use every member. ngaphambili, umlenze, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu is included. 俌 is included. Neither is asked to disappear so the other can be admired.
practice: Admit one small wrong without a speech about your intentions. Stop when the admission is complete.

z: 俓 ngaphambili, umlenze, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Across generations, envy of the young is fear of being finished. Admiration of the young is how an elder stays in the story without owning it.

practice: Clap, or thank, before you comment. Let the first sound from you be glad.

z: 俕 ngaphambili, umlenze, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
An elder who has been afraid and stayed is a better teacher than an elder who claims never to have shaken. The shaking, survived, is the lesson.

practice: Tell the truth you have been saving, and remain in the room after it is told.

z: 俖 ngaphambili, umlenze, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla

An elder's quiet can be a shelter or a locked door. The young can tell which, by whether they are welcome to come and say nothing beside you.

Some breaks end a household. That too can be told with dignity. Forgiveness then is the refusal to poison the years that follow. The children still have to live in them.

line:
An elder who speaks of the dead by name, without recruiting the young into despair, gives the family its memory and its future in the same breath.

line:
An elder who has looked again, many mornings, is a quiet argument against the lie. Do not turn the elder into a slogan. Let the morning itself be seen.

practice: Open the curtain before you decide what the day is. Let the house see you do it.

z: 傧 ingqe, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
An elder who lays down a feud gives the young a future that is not already written. That is one of the last great gifts a generation can give the next.

line:
Anger is the house defending itself before it has measured the threat. Left alone, it burns the people it meant to keep. The heat is not the enemy. Direction is. Turned, the same heat stands in the doorway so the small ones can sleep.

line:
Pride needs an audience and a person beneath it. Dignity needs neither. Hidden inside pride is the refusal to be nothing. That refusal is good. It becomes poison only when someone else must be smaller for it to stand.

line:
Envy is love of a good thing, twisted until the good thing must shrink. The love was real. That is why it hurts. Turned, the same look becomes admiration, which is fed by another person's light.

z: 傮 ingqe, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Fear is the mind counting what it loves and what it could lose. That count is not a defect. It is proof of attachment, and attachment is how a family exists. Courage is fear that stays in the room.

practice: Tell the truth you have been saving, and remain in the room after it is told.

z: 傯 ingqe, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Greed is the fear that there will not be enough, wearing the mask of appetite. Bread kept in a closed hand goes stale. Generosity is the same hand remembering the table.

practice: Put one thing you were keeping back into the middle of the table.

z: 傰 ingqe, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The tongue is the smallest member and the widest fire. Every tradition that lasted put a guard on it, because a family is made of sentences more than of walls.

practice: If you gave someone a cruel name, retire it today, out loud, and do not use it again.

z: 傶 ingqe, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Contempt is a shortcut. It saves a person from having to look. Inside it is the power it refuses: the power to see a thing clearly. Clear sight is the beginning of thanks.

line:
There is a silence that punishes and a silence that accompanies. They use the same closed mouth. The difference is whether the person has left while remaining in the chair.

line:
Betrayal proves that trust was real, because only a real bond breaks with that sound. Forgiveness is not the pretence that the bowl never cracked. It is gold in the crack, and the decision to eat from that bowl again, slowly.

This is the work of an elder with the young. What you are seeing is ingqe, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla, kept. The turn is not a fog laid over it. 傹 names the page. The page still shows a body that can hold, walk, and stay.
practice: If you were the one who broke trust, say what you did without a speech about why it was almost fair.

z: 傼 ingqe, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Grief is love with nowhere to go. It feels like an evil because it stops the house. It is not an invader. It is a force large enough to be mistaken for one. Compassion is that force sitting down beside someone else.

practice: Answer the ordinary request of a grieving child. Do not make them perform a sadness you recognize.

line:
Despair says the dawn is a lie because the room is dark. The force inside it is the fact that someone is still at the window. Waiting is already a kind of faithfulness, even when it feels like defeat.

practice: Decline the word forever. Keep the true sentence about the pain, and stop before the lie.

line:
Revenge believes that pain can be balanced by being copied. It cannot. The copy multiplies, and the family becomes a ledger. Mercy is the refusal to become the injury.

This is the work of an elder with the young. What you are seeing is izinyembezi, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele, kept. The turn is not a fog laid over it. 傿 names the page. The page still shows a body that can hold, walk, and stay.

z: 僀 izinyembezi, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
A marriage can survive a true no. It cannot survive a no that was only a wound looking for a second body. Protection is the no that guards the bond, not the no that wins the evening.

This is the work of an elder with the young. What you are seeing is izinyembezi, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla, kept. The turn is not a fog laid over it. 僀 names the page. The page still shows a body that can hold, walk, and stay.

z: 僁 izinyembezi, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
A parent who comes down to a child's height does not lose rank. Rank was the costume. The person remains. Dignity is the choice to be seen without requiring worship.

z: 僃 izinyembezi, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
A family that can clap for its own is already rich. The eye is the first thief, and it can be the first blessing. The difference is whether the good is allowed to remain in the other hand.

line:

practice: Hold the doorway. Let the frightened one see that you are not leaving.

line:
Generosity is not the opposite of need. It is need that has remembered other mouths. The first portion, not the remainder, teaches the house what it is.

This is the work of an elder with the young. What you are seeing is izinyembezi, phezulu, ngakwesokudla, kept. The turn is not a fog laid over it. 僈 names the page. The page still shows a body that can hold, walk, and stay.

line:
Healing speech is not sweetness. Sweetness can be a lie. Healing speech is accuracy with mercy. It names the hurt and refuses the insult that wanted to ride along.

line:
What is despised at home is despised twice, because home was the place it should have been safe to be plain. Appreciation is looking that did not turn away.

line:
Cold silence is absence wearing a body. Presence is that silence warmed by staying. Put the object down. Let the eyes finish the sentence the mouth is not ready to speak.

line:
A family that cannot mend becomes a set of strangers who still share a key. Mercy here is not amnesia. It is the refusal to make the break the only story the children inherit.

This is the work of an elder with the young. What you are seeing is izinyembezi, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla, kept. The turn is not a fog laid over it. 僗 names the page. The page still shows a body that can hold, walk, and stay.
practice: Decide, and say, whether the person is still a member. Do not leave them in a fog.

line:

practice: Leave the empty place unspoken-of only if the grieving person wishes it. Otherwise, speak the name.

line:
Hope, in the old sense, is not a mood and not a forecast. It is the small fidelity of looking again. Families are made of that looking: one more morning, one more place set.

practice: Set one place at the table that despair said was pointless. Eat there.

line:

line:
Children learn what strength is from the body that stands between them and the weather. If that body spends itself on them, they learn that love arrives as weather. Turn the heat toward the actual danger.

z: 僠 izinyembezi, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
In a marriage, pride keeps a ledger of who apologized last. Dignity throws the ledger out and keeps the person. You can be wrong and still be whole.

z: 僢 izinyembezi, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Between spouses, envy dresses as criticism. The dress is thin. Under it is the wish to be the one who is praised. Say the praise. Leave the gift where it landed.

practice: Say out loud, in the hearing of the person, the exact good you wished were yours. Then leave it theirs.

z: 僤 izinyembezi, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
In a marriage, fear says, if I tell the truth I will be left. Courage tells the truth and remains seated. The staying is the larger sentence.

practice: Stay until the scared person is breathing slowly. Do not explain the dark away before you have sat in it.

z: 僨 izinyembezi, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
A marriage becomes a grievance when the store is private. What is earned may be stewarded. What is hoarded becomes a wall between two people who share a bed.

practice: Pass the best portion first. The first piece teaches the house what it is.

line:
In a marriage, the second sentence is usually the one that only wanted to win. Speak the first, which is the truth. Keep the second. The keeping is love.

practice: Speak the true sentence. Keep the second one, the one that only wanted to win.

line:
A marriage dies faster from sneering than from anger. Anger still believes the other person matters. Contempt has already left, and only the body remains at the table.

line:
In a marriage, the punishing quiet can last longer than a blow, and it teaches the same lesson: you are alone in this room. Presence refuses to teach that.

Name the break once, plainly, without the extra charges that make you feel righteous. Then do one small trustworthy thing, and do it again tomorrow. Trust is rebuilt at that size.

practice: Bring food. Take the lower seat. Stay past the moment you become uncomfortable.

line:
Open the curtain before you decide what the day is. Let the house see you do it. The gesture is small, and it is the whole teaching.

practice: Make one plan for tomorrow small enough that both of you can keep it.

line:
Do one undeserved kindness to the person you are keeping score against. Do not mention the score. The mention would turn the kindness back into a move.

This is the work of an elder with the young. What you are seeing is izinyembezi, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele, kept. The turn is not a fog laid over it. 僶 names the page. The page still shows a body that can hold, walk, and stay.

z: 僷 izinyembezi, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
The counsel that lasted did not flatter rage. It asked the strong to become a wall for the weak. That is the ethic of a parent and of an elder: your size is a shelter, or it is a threat.

This is the work of an elder with the young. What you are seeing is izinyembezi, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla, kept. The turn is not a fog laid over it. 僷 names the page. The page still shows a body that can hold, walk, and stay.
practice: Before the second loud sentence, step into the doorway, not toward the person. Let the heat guard the house from outside.

z: 僸 izinyembezi, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The old wisdom is severe on the high seat. It is not severe on the upright spine. Stand up. Then let the others stand. A house of one standing person is a court, not a family.

This is the work of an elder with the young. What you are seeing is izinyembezi, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu, kept. The turn is not a fog laid over it. 僸 names the page. The page still shows a body that can hold, walk, and stay.

z: 僺 izinyembezi, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
A child who is envied by a parent carries a weight no child can name. Admiration from above is a kind of safety. It says, your becoming does not threaten my place.

This is the work of an elder with the young. What you are seeing is izinyembezi, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu, kept. The turn is not a fog laid over it. 僺 names the page. The page still shows a body that can hold, walk, and stay.
